newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends slightly up vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends slightly up vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly up at 8.3053 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.3055 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market due to strong pro-yuan sentiment, traders said.
The yuan rose despite intervention by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, to depress the local currency at around the key 8.3050 resistance level, they said.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.3055 and consolidated around its opening price for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.3050 and a low of 8.3057 in mid-session.
Trading was dull, with most done at about 8.3054.
"The central bank intervened when the yuan hit the 8.3050 level," said one trader. "It sold the yuan to stabilise the local currency and prevent it from rising sharply."
"Selling of the yuan by the central bank has prevented it from rising sharply for three successive days," said a second trader. "As a result, it seems difficult for the yuan to rise much this week."
Traders expect the yuan to move around 8.3050 on Thursday.
The yuan ended up at 7.5480 from 7.5850 against 100 Japanese yen on the yen's weakness on the world market. It closed down at an intra-day low of 1.0750 from 1.0735 against the H.K. dollar.
